criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Memo identifies LTV exceeds 80% FFIEC supervisory limit
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum computes the as-is LTV at 81.04% in Section A-3 and states that it is 'outside conventional commercial real estate limits,' recommending a 'documented credit exception.' However, it never identifies the 80% supervisory LTV limit, nor does it reference the federal interagency guidelines (FFIEC / 12 CFR Part 365 or any equivalent regulatory threshold). The memo treats the issue purely as a credit-exception matter rather than a regulatory LTV threshold exceedance, so the specific criterion — identifying that the ~81% as-is LTV exceeds the 80% FFIEC supervisory limit — is not satisfied.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_001: Memo recommends board exception approval for LTV exceedance
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly addresses the 81.04% as-is LTV exceedance at Section A-3 ('As-is LTV of 81.04% requires a documented credit exception'), notes that an 81% as-is LTV is 'outside conventional commercial real estate limits,' and recommends obtaining written confirmation that 'loan committee or the board has approved the exception' and placing it in the closing file. It further notes that a credit exception 'is not a document term and should be evidenced separately,' and lists it as open item #15 requesting confirmation of loan committee or board approval of the 81.04% as-is LTV. This satisfies the criterion's requirement to recommend or note the need for board approval/documentation of an exception for exceeding the ~80% LTV limit.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Mortgage includes specific CREC covenant for vapor barrier
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage contains an explicit, specific covenant at Section 7.6(c)(ii) requiring Mortgagor to 'maintain, repair, preserve and keep in good condition and working order the vapor barrier system installed beneath the concrete floor slab of Bay 1, and shall not penetrate, remove, breach, compromise or render ineffective any portion of such vapor barrier.' Additional specific provisions reinforce this: Section 7.6(c)(iii) conditions any slab-disturbing work on SCDHEC notice and pre/post-work professional certification of barrier integrity; Section 7.6(c)(vii) requires annual certification plus a licensed environmental professional's compliance report; Section 7.6(c)(iv) requires informing contractors (including the GC) of the barrier; Section 10.2(g) makes compliance a condition to Draws affecting the Bay 1 slab; Section 12.1(k)/12.2(c) make breach an immediate Event of Default; and Exhibit E sets out a step-by-step compliance protocol expressly tied to the recorded LUR (Deed Book 1203, Page 89) and SCDHEC Site ID SC-29403-0772. This far exceeds a generic 'comply with environmental laws' covenant, so the criterion is satisfied.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Mortgage prohibits residential conversion of ground floor Lot 7/Bay 1
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage expressly includes a covenant in Section 7.6(c)(i) prohibiting residential use or conversion of the ground floor of Lot 7/Bay 1, and reinforces it with related LUR compliance covenants, definitions, and an Event of Default provision. This satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Breach of CREC/environmental restriction is an event of default
criteria_results.reasoning: The instrument repeatedly ties violation of the SCDHEC Land Use Restriction to an Event of Default. Section 7.6(c) imposes the specific covenants (no residential use of the ground floor of Lot 7, vapor barrier maintenance/no penetration without SCDHEC notice and environmental professional certification), and Section 7.6(f) expressly states that any failure to comply with the Land Use Restriction, any residential use of the Lot 7 ground floor, or any penetration/compromise of the Bay 1 vapor barrier without satisfying Section 7.6(c)(iii) is an immediate Event of Default without notice or cure. Article 12 separately codifies this: Section 12.1(k) lists breach of any Section 7.6 covenant (including the Land Use Restriction and vapor barrier provisions) as an Event of Default, and Section 12.2(c)(iii) confirms no cure period applies. Exhibit E, Step 8 reinforces the same default consequence, and Section 18.14(d) makes such a breach a full-recourse carve-out. Thus the specific restriction is squarely tied to a default provision.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_002: Memo identifies CREC compliance obligation as a drafting issue
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies the Controlled Recognized Environmental Condition on Lot 7, including the petroleum contamination, the vapor barrier beneath the Bay 1 slab, and the SCDHEC land use restriction. It treats this as a Priority 1 drafting issue requiring specific environmental covenants in the Mortgage (Section 7.6), a dedicated uncurable Event of Default (Sections 12.1(k), 12.2(c)), draw conditions tied to SCDHEC notice and pre/post-work certification (Section 10.2(g)), and a GC Contract covenant. It also expressly rejects the partner's instruction that a 'standard template' environmental covenant would suffice, citing Note 1 to closer, Term Sheet §5.4 and the ESA. This fully satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Memo identifies renovation holdback gap ($900K shortfall)
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo expressly identifies the requested gap. Section 6.1 item 11 computes the Renovation Holdback as $14,750,000 − $12,500,000 = $2,250,000, and item 14 allocates the $3,150,000 budget between holdback ($2,250,000) and borrower equity ($900,000). A-4 and A-6 discuss the $900,000 Borrower Equity for Renovation and confirm it is fully committed, and A-7 discusses the draw schedule's equity funding. The $900,000 gap to be funded by borrower equity is therefore identified and discussed at multiple points.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Mortgage requires borrower equity contribution before holdback draws
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage expressly addresses sequencing of borrower equity versus holdback draws. Section 10.2(d) conditions each lender draw on Mortgagor having funded (or deposited/evidenced to Mortgagee’s satisfaction) the allocable portion of the $900,000 Borrower Equity Contribution, and further limits cumulative holdback disbursements to no more than 71.43% of cumulative Renovation Costs then incurred. Section 10.3(f) requires corresponding evidence with each Draw Request, and Section 10.1 states the equity contribution is from Mortgagor’s own funds and not Loan proceeds. This satisfies the criterion by requiring borrower equity to be contributed in sequence with, and ahead of, lender holdback funding to protect the lender.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_003: Memo flags draw schedule shows interspersed (not equity-first) funding
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum discusses the draw schedule and notes a pro-rata funding test, but it does not flag that borrower equity contributions are interspersed with lender draws rather than required to be contributed first. In fact, it states that equity is funded ahead of entitlement throughout and treats that as favourable to Lender. It also does not identify the specific risk that the holdback could be exhausted before completion due to interspersed funding. Therefore the criterion is not satisfied.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Memo identifies Harmon & Wren ROFR on Bay 2 conflict with leasing covenants
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies in F-4 that Harmon & Wren Design Studio LLC holds a ROFR on Bay 2, that it is exercisable within 15 business days of a bona fide third-party offer, that it survives renewal of the Bay 3 lease, and that any Bay 2 lease must be sequenced around it. It further explains the interaction with the leasing covenant in Section 7.3 and the need to obtain Lender approval of Bay 2 lease terms before presenting them to Harmon & Wren so the ROFR mechanics do not later change the deal. This satisfies the criterion by identifying the ROFR and its constraining effect on lease-up/leasing covenants.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_004: Mortgage addresses ROFR in leasing covenant provisions
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage expressly addresses the Harmon & Wren ROFR on Bay 2 in multiple places: Section 7.3 contains a dedicated 'Tenant right of first refusal' paragraph requiring Mortgagee approval of material terms before presenting third-party offers, delivery of offers/waivers/resulting leases, and noting approval doesn't bind later leases; Section 6.4 represents the ROFR as the only such right affecting the Property; Section 5.6 references it; Exhibit B (Permitted Exceptions, item 4) acknowledges it as an existing encumbrance; and Exhibit D discloses it. This satisfies the criterion's requirement to acknowledge the ROFR, accommodate it in the leasing covenant, and require compliance as a condition of leasing Bay 2.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Memo identifies missing assignment consent clause in Lowcountry Provisions lease
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies in F-1 that the Lowcountry Provisions lease is silent on assignment/subletting and lacks any assignment consent requirement. It then discusses the lender's assignment-of-rents structure, including the representation of authority to assign that lease (Section 5.2(e)) and the bankruptcy/recharacterization implications of an absolute assignment of rents (F-3), satisfying the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Mortgage/memo recommends estoppel certificate from Lowcountry Provisions
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage expressly requires estoppel certificates: Section 5.6 obligates Mortgagor to obtain estoppel certificates from each Tenant in accordance with Term Sheet §12.1 and specifically states that Mortgagor shall cause Lowcountry Provisions Inc. to deliver an estoppel certificate and SNDA as a condition to closing (with a post-closing covenant to add estoppel obligations at renewal, outside date March 31, 2027). Section 12.1(r) makes failure to deliver a required estoppel or SNDA an Event of Default. The issues memorandum likewise recommends obtaining the Lowcountry estoppel (F-1, B-9, open item 12), addressing the tenant's lack of any contractual estoppel obligation in connection with the absolute assignment of rents.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_005: Mortgage includes borrower representation re right to assign rents
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage expressly includes a borrower representation and warranty in Section 5.2 that Mortgagor is the owner and has the full right, power, and authority to absolutely and presently assign each Lease and all Rents, and that it has not previously assigned or encumbered them. This directly satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Memo identifies gap between SPE requirements and operating agreement
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly and repeatedly identifies the gap between the SPE requirements and the borrower's operating agreement. Executive Summary item 3 states the operating agreement 'does not support the SPE structure' — no independent manager, no separateness covenants, no single-purpose purpose clause, no lender consent to dissolution or amendment, and bankruptcy is not a 'Major Decision.' Section D-1 contains a detailed table showing each required SPE provision is 'Absent' under the OA, D-2 explains that bankruptcy is not a Major Decision (defeating bankruptcy remoteness), and the memo makes the Operating Agreement Amendment, member consents and joinders an express closing condition (Sections 6.12, 7.4, 7.4(i), 7.4(j)), with the amendment to be drafted by Borrower's counsel (D-1, D-8, open items 3–4). The criterion is fully satisfied.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Mortgage includes SPE covenants with independent director requirement
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage includes express single-purpose entity covenants in Section 7.4, including a requirement in Section 7.4(h) that certain bankruptcy, dissolution, merger, or liquidation actions require the affirmative vote of an independent manager/director, and Section 7.4(k) requires Mortgagor to maintain an independent manager or independent director at all times. Section 6.12 also requires an independent manager/director provision in the operating agreement. This satisfies the independent director/manager requirement for bankruptcy remoteness.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_006: Memo flags need for passive member consent to SPE restrictions
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly addresses the need for passive member consent and joinder. Section 3.4 makes 'the executed operating agreement amendment, together with the written consent and joinder of all three members' an express closing condition. D-5 ('Member consents and authority') states that 'The SPE covenants and transfer restrictions must bind all three members, not only GDG' and identifies authority gaps requiring resolutions/certificates from Tidewater GP Holdings LLC (general partner of Tidewater Opportunity Fund II LP) and Harborline Capital Advisors LLC. The Executive Summary (Section 2) also flags that 'The SPE amendments (D-1) must be signed by all three members.' The criterion is satisfied.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Mortgage includes flood insurance covenant for $5M in Zone X
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage's Article 8 insurance covenant expressly requires flood insurance. Section 8.1(c) obligates Mortgagor to maintain 'Flood insurance on the Property in an amount not less than $5,000,000, naming Mortgagee as mortgagee and loss payee, notwithstanding that the Property is located in FEMA Flood Zone X.' This requirement is reinforced by the policy requirements in Section 8.2 and reaffirmed in Exhibit E, Part 3 ('Flood insurance of not less than $5,000,000 is nevertheless required under Section 8.1(c)'). The criterion requires at least $5,000,000 of flood insurance in Zone X, which is exactly what the document provides.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_007: Memo or mortgage distinguishes contractual vs. regulatory flood insurance
criteria_results.reasoning: Both documents explicitly make the distinction. The issues memorandum (C-4 and H-4) states that the $5,000,000 flood requirement in FEMA Zone X is a Lender-imposed contractual condition, 'notwithstanding that federal regulation does not require it.' The Mortgage itself (Section 8.1(c)) requires flood insurance 'notwithstanding that the Property is located in FEMA Flood Zone X and that flood insurance is not required by federal regulation,' and expressly characterizes the coverage as 'a condition of the Loan imposed by Mortgagee in its sole discretion.' Exhibit E likewise notes the coverage is 'nevertheless required' in Zone X. The criterion is satisfied.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Memo identifies balcony encroachment over King Street ROW
criteria_results.reasoning: Section B-3 is expressly titled 'Balcony encroachment' and identifies that a decorative iron balcony projects approximately 2.5 feet over the King Street right-of-way, citing Title Commitment Exception 5 and the appraisal. It notes the absence of any encroachment permit, license or franchise in the record, the Title Insurer's recommendation of ALTA Endorsement 28.1, and the appraiser's recommendation to confirm the permit and assess removal risk; it also ties the encroachment to the façade restoration scope and BAR approval and implements a covenant (Section 7.16). Open item 9 in Section 7 additionally requests the encroachment permit or written confirmation that none exists. All elements of the criterion are satisfied.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_008: Mortgage includes covenant to maintain encroachment permit/license
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 7.16 ("Preservation of Permits, Easements and Encroachment Rights") expressly requires the borrower to obtain and thereafter maintain in effect any encroachment license, franchise, permit or other authorization from the City of Charleston for the decorative iron balcony extending ~2.5 feet over the King Street right-of-way, to deliver copies of applications/correspondence/approvals, and to notify Mortgagee of any City notice. It further prohibits removing or altering the balcony except per approved Plans and Specifications and BAR approval, which prevents exacerbation of the encroachment. Article 2.1(a)/(b), 6.5, and Exhibit B Exception 5 corroborate this treatment. The criterion is satisfied.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Yield maintenance formula specifies which U.S. Treasury rate is used
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 16.2 defines the Treasury Rate with specificity: the yield to maturity of the U.S. Treasury security having a maturity closest to, but not exceeding, the last day of the Yield Maintenance Period, based on the Federal Reserve H.15 Treasury Constant Maturities, with linear interpolation between nearest published maturities if necessary. This satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Yield maintenance formula includes the 50 basis point spread
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 16.2 of the mortgage defines the Yield Maintenance Premium with clause (b) computing interest at "the Treasury Rate plus fifty (50) basis points (0.50%)," and further states the amount under clause (b) is zero if the Note rate is less than or equal to the Treasury Rate plus 50 bps. The 50 basis point spread is expressly included in the formula.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Yield maintenance formula provides a calculable methodology
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 16.2 of the mortgage sets out a complete, self-contained yield maintenance formula. It identifies the premium as the greater of (a) 1.00% of the principal prepaid and (b) a rate-differential present-value calculation, and then specifies the mechanics in detail: (i) the discount rate—the 'Treasury Rate'—is expressly defined as the yield to maturity on the U.S. Treasury security with a maturity closest to (but not exceeding) the last day of the Yield Maintenance Period, taken from Federal Reserve Statistical Release H.15 'Treasury Constant Maturities' two Business Days before prepayment, with linear interpolation between the two nearest published maturities if no exact match exists; (ii) the calculation is described step by step—present value, discounted monthly, of the interest that would have accrued at the Note rate over the remaining Yield Maintenance Period, minus the present value, discounted monthly, of interest at the Treasury Rate plus 50 bps, floored at zero (and zero if the Note rate is at or below Treasury + 50 bps); and (iii) the discounting convention is prescribed (monthly periodic rate equal to Treasury Rate divided by twelve, applied over the number of whole and partial months remaining), along with a fallback if the Treasury Rate is unpublished and a provision for a written calculation from Mortgagee. A third party could compute the premium from these provisions alone without further negotiation or interpretation, satisfying both prongs (a) and (b) of the criterion. Note also that this is far more than the prohibited shorthand (e.g., 'Treasury rate + 50 bps' alone).

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_009: Memo identifies yield maintenance ambiguity in term sheet
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum discusses yield maintenance extensively, including a defect in the Markup Notes formula, the placement of the 50 basis points, the 1% floor, and enforceability under South Carolina law. It also states that the Mortgage defines the Treasury Rate precisely. However, it does not explicitly identify that the Term Sheet's yield maintenance description is ambiguous because it fails to specify which Treasury rate applies, nor does it frame that ambiguity as an issue that must be resolved in the Mortgage to avoid an unenforceable penalty. The enforceability discussion is general and tied to specificity, but the specific Term Sheet ambiguity regarding the Treasury rate is not identified as required by the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Mortgage transfer restrictions cover indirect/fund-level changes
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 7.5(c) expressly addresses 'Indirect and upstream transfers,' deeming any change in Control of Mortgagor, of Graydon Development Group LLC, or of any Person that Controls Mortgagor — whether by equity transfer, merger, admission or withdrawal of a general partner or managing member, proxy/voting agreement, or otherwise — a Transfer requiring Mortgagee's consent. It further specifically prohibits transfers of Graydon Development Group LLC's interest in the borrower, indirect ownership changes at Graydon, and transfers of Tidewater Opportunity Fund II LP's interest to any successor fund managed by or affiliated with Tidewater GP Holdings LLC. Related provisions (Section 7.4(j)) require Tidewater GP Holdings LLC, as GP, to acknowledge and be bound by the SPE Covenants and transfer restrictions, and the borrower's members (Graydon, Tidewater, Harborline) are named. Harborline's member/manager-level changes are captured by the 'any Person that Controls Mortgagor' and change-of-Control language. This satisfies the criterion's requirement for indirect/upstream change-of-control coverage, not merely direct borrower-interest transfers.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: Memo identifies transfer restriction gap re fund-level changes
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo identifies the transfer-restriction gap at the fund/member level. Section D-3 explains that OA §4.2(c) permits Tidewater to transfer its 18% interest to any 'successor fund' managed by Tidewater GP Holdings LLC or an Affiliate without consent, which conflicts with Term Sheet §10.3's 10%/25% limits and its 'existing members only' exception. Section D-4 explains that OA §4.1 reaches only transfers of membership interests in the Company, not 'changes in the internal or upstream ownership or management of any member,' so Mr. Graydon could transfer his GDG interest or 'Tidewater GP Holdings LLC could itself be acquired or replaced.' Section D-5 further notes that Tidewater GP Holdings LLC is the general partner of Tidewater Opportunity Fund II LP, highlighting the GP-level authority issue. The cross-reference table (6.3 item 12) repeats the conflict between TS §10.3 and OA §§4.2(c), 4.1. Proposed mitigant is Section 7.5(c) (deemed change of Control) and a conforming amendment (Section 7.5(d)). This satisfies the criterion's requirement to flag that the term-sheet transfer language may not capture GP/LP-composition or upstream control changes.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_010: 'Existing members' exception is narrowly defined
criteria_results.reasoning: The transfer restriction exception in Section 7.5(b) specifically identifies the three existing members—Graydon Development Group LLC, Tidewater Opportunity Fund II LP, and Harborline Capital Advisors LLC—and further narrows the exception by requiring no change of Control, prior notice, and continued SPE status/no change in Managing Member. This satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Memo identifies tight timeline between completion and DSCR testing
criteria_results.reasoning: The memo squarely identifies the timing concern. Section G-8 ('The ten-month unguarded gap') states that the interest-shortfall guaranty covers only the first 14 months, that Substantial Completion is due at month 14, that the first DSCR test is at month 24, and that 'Between month 15 and month 24 there is neither a guaranty of debt service nor a tested covenant,' expressly tying the gap to the lease-up period (Suite B rent commencing February 1, 2027). Executive-summary risk item 11 repeats this ('Months 15–24 are unguarded and untested — and that is precisely when lease-up risk concentrates'). Current in-place income insufficiency is also documented in A-2, which shows NOI of $622,772 against required NOI of $1,078,594 (interest-only) or $1,405,299 (amortizing), yielding 0.72x/0.55x versus the 1.25x covenant. The memo further notes the internal conflict on the exact first test date (Term Sheet literal July 15, 2027 versus April 15, 2027 in borrower materials), but the 10-month completion-to-testing gap and the income shortfall are both clearly discussed.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_011: Mortgage includes DSCR cure mechanism or cash sweep provision
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage includes a DSCR covenant in Section 7.8(a) and makes a DSCR below 1.25 for two consecutive quarters an Event of Default under Section 12.1(i). However, it provides no cash sweep, additional reserve deposit, equity cure right, or other mechanism to address a DSCR shortfall at the initial test date. The cure provisions do not provide a DSCR cure, so the covenant operates as a hard default without a protective mechanism.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Memo identifies chain of title concern for vacated Anson Lane strip
criteria_results.reasoning: The memorandum expressly identifies the Anson Lane strip as conveyed by quitclaim deed recorded in Deed Book 1128, Page 443, flags the resulting chain-of-title concern and disclaimed equivalence, and recommends affirmative title insurance confirmation and endorsement. This satisfies the criterion.

criteria_results.title: ISSUE_012: Mortgage legal description includes Anson Lane strip
criteria_results.reasoning: Exhibit A of the mortgage includes 'PARCEL TWO (Vacated Anson Lane Strip),' which expressly references vacation by City of Charleston Ordinance No. 2019-084 and the quitclaim deed recorded in Deed Book 1128 at Page 443, together with the survey/plat reference. The strip is also described in Section 2.1(a) of the granting clause. The criterion (inclusion of the Anson Lane strip in the legal description) is satisfied, notwithstanding the placeholder note that metes and bounds will be inserted prior to recording.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage identifies borrower entity type and address

criteria_results.title: Mortgage states correct loan amount of $14,750,000
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage repeatedly and consistently states the loan amount as $14,750,000: the header lists 'PRINCIPAL AMOUNT SECURED: $14,750,000.00'; Recital A states the Loan is in the original principal amount of $14,750,000; the definitions of 'Loan' and 'Note' use $14,750,000; Section 2.5 states the Indebtedness secured is $14,750,000; and the Title Policy amount is $14,750,000. The disbursement structure ($12,500,000 Initial Advance + $2,250,000 Renovation Holdback) also sums to $14,750,000. No conflicting loan amount appears.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage states correct maturity date of April 15, 2030
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage expressly states the maturity date as April 15, 2030 in the cover summary ("MATURITY DATE: April 15, 2030") and in the definition of "Maturity Date" in Section 1.1 ("means April 15, 2030"). This is 5 years from the April 15, 2025 closing/instrument date, and is consistent with the related provisions (interest-only through April 2027, 25-year amortization thereafter, yield maintenance through the 48th monthly anniversary, open prepayment in the final 12 months). No incorrect maturity date appears.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage states interest rate as Daily SOFR + 285 bps
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage expressly defines the 'Applicable Rate' as the sum of (a) Daily SOFR (subject to a 3.00% SOFR Floor) plus (b) two hundred eighty-five basis points (2.85%), and the definition is referenced throughout (interest computation, default rate, benchmark replacement). The benchmark (Daily SOFR) and spread (285 bps) are both correctly stated and not missing.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage states SOFR floor of 3.00%
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage explicitly defines 'SOFR Floor' as three percent (3.00%) per annum in Article 1 and references it in the Applicable Rate definition, stating that Daily SOFR shall be no less than the SOFR Floor of 3.00%. Therefore, the criterion is satisfied.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage states correct default rate: applicable rate + 5.00%
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage expressly defines the Default Rate as the Applicable Rate plus five percent (5.00%) per annum in the definitions and Section 15.3, satisfying the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes 24-month interest-only period from closing
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 15.1(b) of the mortgage expressly provides that the Loan is interest-only for the first twenty-four (24) months following the Closing Date, with monthly payments consisting solely of accrued interest, and amortization beginning May 15, 2027 (Section 15.1(c)). The 24-month IO period from closing is therefore present and correctly stated.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes 25-year amortization schedule after IO period
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 15.1(c) of the mortgage expressly provides that, commencing with the payment due May 15, 2027 (after the 24-month interest-only period), monthly payments of principal and interest are due based on a twenty-five (25) year amortization schedule, calculated on the then-outstanding principal balance and then-applicable interest rate. The IO period is defined in Section 15.1(b) (first 24 months following Closing), and the sequence is consistent with the Maturity Date of April 15, 2030. The 25-year amortization schedule is clearly stated and not omitted or incorrect.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes 24-month lockout period with no prepayment
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage expressly defines a Lockout Period running from the Closing Date through the day before the 24th monthly anniversary of the Note date and prohibits voluntary prepayment in whole or in part during that period. Article 16.1 states no prepayment is permitted during the Lockout Period, satisfying the 24-month lockout requirement.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes yield maintenance premium prepayment from month 25 through month 48
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage expressly provides a Lockout Period ending on the day before the 24th monthly anniversary of the Note, and then a Yield Maintenance Period running from the expiration of the Lockout Period through the 48th monthly anniversary of the Note. Section 16.2 permits prepayment during that period subject to the Yield Maintenance Premium. This matches the required month 25 through month 48 yield maintenance premium prepayment structure.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes open prepayment with no premium during final 12 months
criteria_results.reasoning: Article 16, Section 16.3 expressly provides an open prepayment period during the final twelve months of the Loan term (from after the 48th monthly anniversary through maturity) permitting prepayment in whole or in part without any prepayment premium, penalty, or yield maintenance. This satisfies the criterion for months 49–60.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes late charge of 5% with 10-day grace period
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 15.4 provides for a Late Charge equal to 5.00% of any overdue installment not received within ten (10) calendar days after its due date, matching the criterion.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes DSCR covenant of at least 1.25x tested quarterly
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage includes an express DSCR covenant in Section 7.8(a) requiring a Debt Service Coverage Ratio of not less than 1.25 to 1.00, tested as of the last day of each calendar quarter and continuing quarterly thereafter. This satisfies the criterion's minimum ratio and quarterly testing requirement.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage DSCR testing commences 24 months after closing
criteria_results.reasoning: The mortgage provides in Section 7.8(a) that DSCR testing commences with the calendar quarter ending June 30, 2027, described as the first full calendar quarter ending after the 24th month following the Closing Date. This matches the criterion's permitted quarter-end following month 24.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes tax and insurance escrow provision
criteria_results.reasoning: Article 9.1 of the mortgage expressly requires Mortgagor to deposit with Mortgagee, on the Closing Date and thereafter on each Payment Date, an amount equal to one-twelfth (1/12) of the estimated annual Impositions (real property taxes on all three parcels) and Insurance Premiums, with the funds held in escrow and applied to those obligations, deficiency funding obligations, and Mortgagee's right to advance shortfalls. This satisfies the criterion for a monthly 1/12 tax and insurance escrow provision.

criteria_results.title: Mortgage includes capital replacement reserve of $0.25/SF/year
criteria_results.reasoning: Section 9.2 of the mortgage establishes a Capital Replacement Reserve requiring monthly deposits of $645.83, expressly calculated as $0.25 per square foot per year × 31,000 SF = $7,750/year ÷ 12 months.
